Review `README.md` and `/src` for repository purpose/structure and update this overview accordingly.

**Framework:** .NET 10.0 (`net10.0`); latest C#; nullable and implicit usings enabled; `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`; XML documentation warning 1591 suppressed via `NoWarn`. All projects inherit [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props). Use analyzers there; consider NSDepCop.

**Structure:** `src/` production, `tests/` tests, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `Template.slnx`. Central package management is enabled (`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true`); versions belong in [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props), and project references omit versions. Add packages with `<PackageVersion Include="PackageName" Version="x.y.z" />`.

**Style:** Use file-scoped namespaces outside namespace (`namespace MyProject.Feature;`), 2-space indentation, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM, Allman braces, and braces except single-line exits. Private fields use `_myField`; constants PascalCase; `var` for built-in/apparent types; interfaces `I`; async methods `Async`. Prefer primary constructors (ALWAYS assign to readonly fields), top-level entry points, pattern matching, and expression-bodied properties/indexers/accessors (not methods). Run `dotnet format`.

Use `appsettings.json` and `appsettings.{Environment}.json`; use `IConfiguration`, `IOptions<T>`, strongly typed settings, and User Secrets. Never hardcode sensitive information in source code. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, suitable levels, context, structured logging, correlation IDs where possible, and avoid sensitive data.

Use `Ardalis.GuardClauses` for non-UI validation and prefer `FluentValidation` for complex/UI validation. UI invalid input must produce user-friendly errors; non-UI invalid input must throw appropriate guard-clause exceptions. Return suitable HTTP status codes. Follow OWASP: validate/sanitize inputs, parameterized queries/ORM, authentication/authorization, HTTPS.

Write unit-testable code. Offer to add applicable tests in `tests/`; only test controlled business logic, not framework code. Use focused classes, DI, composition, async I/O, short methods (ideally under 20 lines), and parameter objects above 4 arguments. Prefer FastEndpoints `REPR`, DDD, DTOs, and suffixes: `*Request`/`*Response`, `*Command`/`*Query`, `*Details`/`*Summary`. Avoid interfaces and implementations in the same project.

New projects: production in `src/`, tests in `tests/`; test projects use `xUnit`. Run:
`dotnet run --project src/YourProject/YourProject.csproj`

Use xUnit, Arrange-Act-Assert with whitespace only, feature-mirroring folders, `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`/`[InlineData]`, NSubstitute, and Shouldly. Do not name test classes with "Tests" suffix; use "Tests" suffix for folders. Name classes `ClassName_MethodName.cs`; methods `DoesSomething_GivenSomeCondition`, forming a sentence. Example: `ProductServiceTests/ProductService_Constructor.cs`, `ProductService_Constructor._ReturnsInstanceGivenValidInputs`. Separate unit/integration tests. Avoid commercially licensed testing libraries (e.g. FluentAssertions, Moq).

Documentation: Markdown, headings, highlighted code, blank lines around lists/code listings; run linting tools. See [.editorconfig](.editorconfig), [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props), [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props), and [.gitignore](.gitignore).
